title: FIX-FIRST: release-profile fail-open — panic=abort defeats catch_unwind, re-prove crash fixtures against a release binary
action: P1 repair (validation decision 2026-07-26). crates/Cargo.toml:17 sets `panic = "abort"` on [profile.release], while the hook fail-open contract is implemented with std::panic::catch_unwind (crates/queen-bee/src/hooks/write_guard.rs:684 and :950, plus the run_fail_open wrapper). Cargo test targets build with the test/dev profile (panic=unwind), so every existing fail-open green — rust-port-7/9/10/11/12 crash fixtures — proves a profile the host never ships: in a real release binary a panic ABORTS (SIGABRT / exit 134) instead of exiting 0 with a hooks.jsonl crash line, so the guard would kill the turn it exists to protect. Same failure class as the vendoring-drift pattern: the test ran a different artifact than production. CRASH-TRIGGER SEAM (advisor note 1 — read this before designing the proof): the existing Rust crash fixture (crates/queen-bee/tests/hook_conformance.rs:568-586) is a HANDLED I/O fault absorbed via Result — it never unwinds, exits 0 under BOTH profiles, and therefore can neither satisfy red-first nor exercise catch_unwind. This cell must establish a real unwind trigger, and the choice is named here rather than improvised: add an INERT, env-gated deliberate-panic seam to the shipped binary (e.g. a fixture-only env var the hook runtime checks and panics on, documented in the source as test-only, never reachable without that env var), or find a genuinely panicking input and document it. FIX: make the release artifact honor the fail-open contract — remove `panic = "abort"` from [profile.release] (members list untouched; note the cold-start/size cost in the report and measure it), OR keep abort and make every hook path panic-free by construction; whichever is chosen, the proof requirement below is the same. PROOF (the load-bearing half): add a release-profile crash conformance target that spawns the ACTUAL crates/target/release/queen-bee binary (built with the release profile, not a test-profile harness), triggers the seam, and asserts exit code 0 plus the hooks.jsonl crash line — one per hook that owns a crash contract. RED-FIRST is mandatory and environment-independent: with the pre-fix profile the same target must FAIL (non-zero/abort observed), recorded verbatim in the trace, before the fix makes it pass.

truths: cargo --test release_failopen runs and reports at least 4 passed, spawning the real crates/target/release/queen-bee binary (not a test-profile harness)
the crash trigger genuinely unwinds (a handled Result-absorbed fault does not satisfy this cell) and is inert without its fixture-only env gate
each crash fixture: release binary exits 0 and appends a hooks.jsonl crash line
red-first recorded: the same target fails against the pre-fix release profile, with the observed abort/exit status quoted in the trace
existing suites (hook_conformance, writeguard_core/bash/read, modelguard_conformance) stay green after the profile change

trace.outcome: release-profile fail-open fix: dropped panic=abort from [profile.release] (panic=unwind, members untouched), added a fixture-only crash_seam_panic_if_armed env-gated panic seam in write_guard.rs (called from both write-guard and model-guard run() closures), and a new release_failopen conformance target that spawns the real target/release/queen-bee binary — red-first proved the pre-fix binary aborts (no exit code, no crash line) instead of failing open, green post-fix (7/7); existing hook_conformance/writeguard_core/writeguard_bash/writeguard_read/modelguard_conformance suites stay green (84 passed).

trace.verify_output:
RED-FIRST (pre-fix, panic="abort" still in [profile.release]):
`cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bee` succeeded (build itself doesn't fail under abort).
`cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bee --test release_failopen` => test result: FAILED. 3 passed; 4 failed.
The 4 failures were exactly the crash-seam-armed fixtures:
  write_guard_release_binary_fails_open_on_armed_crash_seam: assertion left==right failed: left: None right: Some(0)
    (stderr showed the panic message, then the child process had NO exit code at all -- killed by SIGABRT, not a clean exit(0))
  write_guard_release_binary_crash_seam_logs_hooks_jsonl_crash_line: "expected a crash log line naming the armed seam, got []"
    (log_crash never ran -- the process aborted before catch_unwind's Err arm could execute)
  model_guard_release_binary_fails_open_on_armed_crash_seam: same left:None/right:Some(0) shape
  model_guard_release_binary_crash_seam_logs_hooks_jsonl_crash_line: same "got []" shape
The 3 passing tests (inert-without-env-gate x2, mismatched-hook-name) were unaffected by the defect, confirming the failures are specific to the abort behavior, not test-harness noise.

FIX: crates/Cargo.toml [profile.release] panic="abort" -> panic="unwind" (members list untouched).
Binary size cost: 934544 bytes (abort) -> 1031064 bytes (unwind), +96520 bytes (~+10.3%).
